name: AHP / FAHP Spatial Analyzer for ArcGIS Pro
description: An ArcGIS Pro add-in for multi-criteria decision analysis: AHP and fuzzy AHP weights from a pairwise matrix, consistency checking, reclassification, weighted-overlay suitability maps and Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis, all in one dockpane.
about: Runs the whole Analytic Hierarchy Process inside ArcGIS Pro as one dockpane under an MCDA Tools tab, instead of spreadsheets plus Weighted Sum.
Pick criteria rasters from the map, fill the upper triangle of the pairwise matrix (reciprocals are computed) or import it from CSV.
Classical AHP uses the eigenvector (power) method; fuzzy AHP uses triangular fuzzy numbers with Chang's extent analysis or Buckley's geometric mean.
Consistency ratio from Saaty's random index, flagged above 0.10.
Reclassification manager puts unclassified rasters on a 1 to 5 or 1 to 10 scale with equal, geometric, defined or manual intervals.
One click runs the bundled Python toolbox (Spatial Analyst Weighted Sum) and adds the suitability raster to the map.
Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis perturbs one criterion's weight across N runs to show how stable the ranking is.
C# and WPF on the ArcGIS Pro SDK, MIT licence, citation file and a methodology document with the full mathematics, so it can be cited in a thesis.
requirements: ArcGIS Pro 3.5 or later on Windows, with the Spatial Analyst extension licensed
.NET 8.0 Desktop Runtime, which ArcGIS Pro 3.5 and later already require
At least three criteria rasters in the same coordinate system and cell size, pre-classified or raw
To install: close ArcGIS Pro, double-click the .esriAddinX file, click Install Add-in, then open the MCDA Tools tab
To build from source: Visual Studio 2022 and the Esri.ArcGISPro.Extensions30 NuGet package 3.5 or later
licensing: Free and open source under the MIT licence. If you use it in research, cite: Ashfaq, T. (2026). AHP/FAHP Spatial Analyzer for ArcGIS Pro (Version 1.0.0) [Computer software]. The repository has a Cite this repository button. Bugs and feature requests go to the GitHub issues page.

figures.caption: The AHP Analysis dockpane in ArcGIS Pro: criteria on the left, the pairwise comparison matrix in the centre, sensitivity analysis on the right.
A fuzzy AHP suitability raster produced by the add-in, added straight to the map.

name: QGIS
description: The free desktop GIS used across the course. Install the long-term release for coursework.
about: Complete desktop GIS: reads nearly every vector and raster format through GDAL, edits with snapping and topology, and prints map layouts.
Processing toolbox hosts GRASS, SAGA and GDAL algorithms, so one install gives several hundred tools.
Python built in through the console and plugin system; plugins add Semi-Automatic Classification, QuickMapServices basemaps and DataPlotly charts.
The software most Pakistani employers now run alongside or instead of ArcGIS, and the one you can keep using after graduation without a licence.
Two versions at any time: install the long-term release (LTR) unless a tutorial says otherwise; the latest release has newer features and more surprises.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit; macOS 12 or later; or any current Linux distribution
4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB recommended for raster work
About 2 GB of disk space for the install, plus space for your data
A graphics driver with OpenGL 2.0 support; integrated graphics are fine
On Windows use the standalone installer (.msi), not OSGeo4W, unless you need a custom GDAL build

figures.caption: QGIS 3: a styled map with the layer panel, browser and Processing toolbox. Screenshot from the QGIS project repository (GPL).

name: ArcGIS Pro
description: Esri's current desktop GIS. Installers for 3.7 and 3.6 are mirrored for students who hold a licence through the institute.
about: 64-bit successor to ArcMap and the desktop half of Esri's platform, with 2D and 3D mapping in one project and a ribbon interface.
Geoprocessing tools run from the toolbox or from Python through arcpy; a single .aprx file holds maps, layouts, toolboxes and connections.
Strong points: depth of the geoprocessing library, cartography and layouts, sharing to ArcGIS Online, and extensions for network, spatial statistics, imagery and 3D.
Run by most government departments, NESPAK and the large consultancies in Pakistan; the Esri certificate is the one job adverts name.
Choose 3.7 unless a course or plugin needs 3.6. Both need a licence before they open; the installer is Esri's own and nothing here unlocks it.
requirements: Windows 11 or Windows 10 (version 22H2 or later), 64-bit; Windows Server 2019 or later also supported
Processor with at least four cores; eight or more recommended for imagery and 3D
8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB recommended, 32 GB for large rasters and scene layers
32 GB of free disk space, SSD strongly recommended
DirectX 12 capable graphics card with 4 GB of dedicated memory; 8 GB for 3D scenes
Microsoft .NET Desktop Runtime 8, which the installer prompts for if missing
Screen resolution of 1024 x 768 or higher; a 1080p display is realistic for the ribbon
licensing: The institute holds an education licence. Sign in with a named-user account on the university's ArcGIS Online organisation, or ask the GIS lab for a single-use authorisation file. If you have no account, request one from the lab coordinator with your registration number. Esri also offers a free Learn ArcGIS trial for course MOOCs, which lasts for the duration of the course.

name: ArcGIS Desktop (ArcMap) 10.8.2
description: The retired 32-bit ArcMap, still used in older labs and by some departments. Society mirror of the 10.8.2 installer below; use ArcGIS Pro for new work.
about: Previous generation of Esri's desktop software: ArcMap for 2D mapping and editing, ArcCatalog for data management, ArcScene and ArcGlobe for 3D.
32-bit and single-threaded for most tools; uses .mxd documents rather than projects.
Esri ended support on 1 March 2026: no more fixes, and it will not open newer ArcGIS Pro formats.
Still installed in some labs because older tutorials and departmental workflows in Pakistan were written for it.
Learn it only if a course requires it; learn ArcGIS Pro for everything else.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (the application itself is 32-bit)
4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB recommended
About 5 GB of disk space
Microsoft .NET Framework 4.5 or later
A graphics card with 24-bit colour; 3D extensions need OpenGL 2.0
licensing: Needs a licence from the institute's education site licence, either an ArcGIS Administrator single-use authorisation or a concurrent licence from the lab's licence manager. Ask the lab coordinator.

name: ENVI
description: NV5's image analysis software, the standard commercial package for classification, spectral analysis and hyperspectral work.
about: Built around the spectral side of remote sensing: reads imagery from almost every satellite and airborne sensor.
Radiometric and atmospheric correction (FLAASH and QUAC), supervised and unsupervised classification, change detection, spectral unmixing, target detection and hyperspectral analysis.
Feature extraction module does object-based segmentation and classification.
Runs on IDL so every tool can be scripted; newer versions also expose the ENVI API to Python, and ENVI Modeler chains tools into a graph without code.
Faster and better documented than SNAP or QGIS for spectral work; most Pakistani remote sensing theses of the last two decades were produced with it.
Version 6.5 is 64-bit with the workflow-based interface. The Deep Learning module is a separate licensed add-on, not included.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit; also available for Linux
8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB or more recommended for hyperspectral cubes
About 5 GB of disk space for the install; imagery needs far more
A graphics card with OpenGL 2.0 support; dedicated memory helps for large displays
Administrator rights for the installer and the licence tool
licensing: ENVI will not run without a licence. The institute's licence is served through the NV5 licence administrator; ask the remote sensing lab for the activation code or licence server address and enter it in the ENVI Licence Administrator after installing.

name: ERDAS IMAGINE 2025
description: Hexagon's image processing suite for photogrammetry, classification, orthorectification and large production workflows.
about: Raster-first remote sensing system in production use since the 1980s.
Image enhancement, mosaicking, orthorectification, pan-sharpening, classification (now with machine-learning operators), radar processing and terrain analysis.
Spatial Modeler is a visual programming environment: drag tools into a graph, chain them, and batch-run across thousands of images.
IMAGINE Photogrammetry (formerly LPS) handles aerial triangulation, DEM extraction and orthophotos, which is why survey organisations and mapping agencies use it.
The 2025 release updates the interface, the sensor model library and the deep learning operators.
In Pakistan it is common where orthophotos and large mosaics are produced; ENVI is stronger for spectral analysis, IMAGINE for production and photogrammetry.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit; Windows Server 2019 or later also supported
16 GB RAM recommended, 32 GB for photogrammetry and large mosaics
About 8 GB of disk space for the install, plus fast storage for imagery
A dedicated OpenGL 4.x graphics card with at least 4 GB of memory for stereo and 3D views
Microsoft .NET Framework 4.8 and Visual C++ runtimes, included with the installer
licensing: Licences are issued through the Hexagon Geospatial Licence Administration tool, either as a node-locked key or from the lab's licence server. Ask the remote sensing lab for the key or server address before installing; the installer alone does not run.

name: ArcGIS Reality Studio
description: Esri's photogrammetry application for turning aerial and drone imagery into true orthos, meshes, point clouds and surface models.
about: Standalone photogrammetry application in Esri's ArcGIS Reality family.

Takes large sets of overlapping drone, aircraft or satellite images, runs aerial triangulation against ground control, and outputs true orthophotos, surface models, dense point clouds and textured meshes.
Outputs load directly into ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online in Esri's scene layer formats.
Built for city- and district-scale projects: tens of thousands of images on a workstation with a strong GPU.
For small drone surveys, WebODM (free) or ArcGIS Drone2Map do the same job with far lower hardware demands.
Typical student uses: the campus 3D model, a true-ortho of a survey area, and checking its surface model against GNSS points.
requirements: Windows 11 or Windows 10 (version 22H2 or later), 64-bit
Eight or more processor cores; this is a workstation product
32 GB RAM minimum, 64 GB or more recommended
An NVIDIA graphics card with CUDA support and at least 8 GB of memory; more memory shortens mesh generation
Fast SSD storage: a medium drone project easily needs 100 GB of working space
Microsoft .NET Desktop Runtime 8
licensing: Reality Studio is licensed as a user type extension on the university's ArcGIS Online organisation. Ask the GIS lab to assign the licence to your named-user account; without it the application opens but will not process.

name: GRASS GIS
description: Raster, vector and terrain analysis powerhouse. Also available inside QGIS through the Processing toolbox.
about: Oldest open-source GIS still in active development, with the deepest raster and terrain toolset.
Hydrology (watersheds, flow accumulation, stream extraction), solar radiation, cost surfaces, landscape metrics, image classification and time-series modules.
Every tool is a command with documented parameters, so it scripts naturally in shell or Python.
Keeps data in its own location and mapset structure rather than opening files directly; confusing at first, but it makes analysis fast and reproducible.
Most students meet it through QGIS, where the GRASS provider exposes the same tools on ordinary files.
Install it standalone for the full module set, large rasters, or the r.watershed and r.sim tools for hydrology and erosion modelling, which have no equal in other free packages.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, macOS 11 or later, or Linux
4 GB RAM minimum; more for large DEMs
About 1 GB of disk space
On Windows, the standalone installer bundles Python and wxPython; the OSGeo4W installer is the alternative

figures.caption: GRASS GIS 8.4 single-window interface with several map displays and the command history. Screenshot from the GRASS GIS website (CC BY-SA).

name: SAGA GIS
description: Fast terrain and hydrological analysis with hundreds of modules, used in hydrology and geomorphology courses.
about: Lightweight GIS written for geoscientists, organised by theme: terrain analysis, grid processing, geostatistics, image classification and climate tools.
Known for speed on large grids and for terrain indices (TWI, LS factor, curvature families, SAGA wetness index) that other packages lack or compute slowly.
Plain interface and its own grid format; every tool is also available through the SAGA provider in QGIS Processing, where most students use it.
Standalone SAGA is worth installing for terrain-heavy projects and for tool chains that batch a whole terrain analysis from one dialog.
No licence cost, runs well on modest laptops, and is portable: unzip and run.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, or Linux
4 GB RAM minimum
Under 500 MB of disk space; the Windows build is a zip that needs no installer
Microsoft Visual C++ runtimes, usually already present

figures.caption: SAGA's interface: tool library and data manager on the left, map view on the right. Screenshot from the SAGA project on SourceForge.

name: ESA SNAP
description: The Sentinel Application Platform for processing Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery.
about: ESA's free toolbox for the Sentinel missions and most other Earth observation sensors.
The standard desktop tool for Sentinel-1 radar: calibration, speckle filtering, terrain correction, interferometry (InSAR) and polarimetry.
Processing graphs can be saved and run in batch from the Graph Processing Tool.
For Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3: resampling, subsetting, band maths, indices, Sen2Cor atmospheric correction and a classification toolbox, all on the .SAFE products you download.
Written in Java and slower than ENVI for display, but the only free package that covers the radar workflow end to end, which matters for monsoon flood mapping when optical imagery is cloud.
The snappy and esa_snappy modules drive it from Python.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, macOS or Linux, 64-bit
8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB recommended for Sentinel-1 interferometry
About 1 GB for the install; each Sentinel-1 scene is 4 to 8 GB, so plan for 50 GB or more of working space
Java is bundled with the installer; do not install it separately
A screen of at least 1280 x 800; the toolbox panels are dense

figures.caption: SNAP Desktop with a product open in the image view and the Product Explorer. Screenshot from the SNAP help pages (ESA, GPL).

name: PostgreSQL with PostGIS
description: Spatial database for the database and web GIS courses. Install PostgreSQL, then add PostGIS from Stack Builder.
about: PostgreSQL is a general-purpose relational database; PostGIS is the extension that adds geometry: spatial types, indexes, several hundred ST_ functions, routing with pgRouting, and raster storage.
The back end of almost every serious web GIS and most organisational data stores; spatial SQL is the single most valuable skill in the GIS Analyst and GIS Developer roadmaps.
Workflow: install PostgreSQL, add PostGIS through Stack Builder, create a database, run CREATE EXTENSION postgis, connect from QGIS, pgAdmin or Python.
Load data with shp2pgsql, the QGIS DB Manager or ogr2ogr; queries that take minutes on shapefiles run in seconds once a spatial index exists.
Learn it with the PostGIS workshop linked above; the whole workshop runs on a laptop with the default install.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, macOS or Linux
4 GB RAM is plenty for coursework; the server is light
About 1 GB of disk space plus your data
Administrator rights to install the Windows service
Remember the postgres superuser password you set during installation; it is needed for every connection

name: QField
description: Take a QGIS project to the field on Android or iOS. Offline capable, GNSS aware.
about: Mobile companion to QGIS: prepare the project on the desktop with layers, forms, symbology and basemaps, then copy it to the phone or sync through QFieldCloud.
In the field, capture points, lines and polygons with the phone's GNSS or an external receiver, fill the same attribute forms, attach photos, and bring the edits back to QGIS.
Works fully offline, which matters in rural survey areas, and supports external RTK receivers over Bluetooth for centimetre work.
QField, a GeoPackage and an attribute form is the standard survey workflow in the Surveying and Precision Agriculture roadmaps.
Install from the Play Store or App Store; the QField Sync plugin in QGIS packages the project.
requirements: Android 9 or later, or iOS 15 or later; a Windows build exists for tablets
A phone with GNSS and at least 3 GB RAM; a large basemap benefits from more storage
QGIS on the desktop with the QField Sync plugin to package projects
For sub-metre accuracy, an external GNSS receiver with Bluetooth

figures.caption: QField on a phone: the map canvas while navigating to a feature. Screenshot from the QField documentation (OPENGIS.ch).

name: WebODM
description: Open-source drone image processing: orthomosaics, DEMs, point clouds and 3D models from UAV photos.
about: Browser interface to OpenDroneMap, a free photogrammetry pipeline.
Upload drone photos, optionally add ground control points, and it produces an orthomosaic, surface and terrain models, a dense point cloud and a textured mesh, each with a viewer.
Plant health indices and volume measurement are built in.
Runs as Docker containers: on Windows install Docker Desktop with WSL 2 first, then start WebODM from a terminal.
Slow on a laptop (a 300-image flight can take an hour or more) but results compare with Pix4D and Agisoft for mapping work.
The paid native Windows installer is a convenience, not a different product; the Docker route is free.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11 with WSL 2 and Docker Desktop, or macOS, or Linux (the simplest)
16 GB RAM recommended; 8 GB works for small flights with the split-merge option
A 64-bit processor; a GPU is optional and only speeds up part of the pipeline
20 GB free for the containers plus 5 to 10 times the size of your photos for working space
Virtualisation enabled in the BIOS for WSL 2

figures.caption: An orthophoto opened in the WebODM map viewer after processing. Screenshot from the OpenDroneMap documentation.

name: Google Earth Pro
description: Free desktop version with historical imagery, KML editing, and area and path measurement.
about: Desktop edition of Google Earth, free since 2015.
Historical imagery slider shows how a site has changed over twenty years of satellite and aerial images.
Draw and measure placemarks, paths and polygons and save them as KML or KMZ for QGIS or ArcGIS.
Imports shapefiles and GPS tracks, exports high-resolution images for reports, records tours, and shows 3D buildings and terrain.
Not an analysis tool and the imagery cannot be downloaded for processing, but used daily for site reconnaissance, ground-truth planning and visual checks of a classified map.
Sign-in is not required.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, macOS 11 or later, or Linux
4 GB RAM
About 2 GB of disk space for the install and cache
A graphics card with OpenGL or DirectX 9 support
An internet connection; imagery streams from Google and only a cache is stored locally

name: R and RStudio
description: R with the sf, terra and tmap packages for spatial statistics and publication-quality figures.
about: R is a programming language for statistics; RStudio (from Posit) is the editor most people use it in.

Spatial packages: sf for vector data (same simple-features model as PostGIS), terra for rasters, tmap and ggplot2 for maps, spdep, gstat and spatialreg for autocorrelation, interpolation and spatial regression.
The standard tool for the statistical side of a thesis: sampling design, accuracy assessment, regression and journal-quality figures.
Python is stronger for deep learning and GIS integration; R is stronger for statistics, reproducible reports (Quarto, R Markdown) and plotting. Many researchers use both.
Install R first from CRAN, then RStudio; packages install from inside R with install.packages(). Geocomputation with R, linked above, is the complete free course.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, macOS 12 or later, or Linux
4 GB RAM minimum, 8 GB for raster work with terra
About 1 GB for R and RStudio plus packages
On Windows, install Rtools as well if a package needs compiling

figures.caption: The four RStudio panes: source editor, console, environment and files/plots/help. Screenshot from the RStudio User Guide (Posit).

name: Pakistan administrative boundaries, including IIOJK
description: National, provincial, district and tehsil polygons that follow the official Survey of Pakistan map, with Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir included as its own feature. Shapefiles in WGS 84 with full metadata.
about: Most boundary files in circulation, GADM and the OCHA common operational datasets included, draw Pakistan without the Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, or draw the Line of Control as if it were an international border. Any map made from them contradicts the official political map of Pakistan published by the Survey of Pakistan, which government departments, universities and most clients in the country expect. This dataset was created to fix that for student and research work.

Four shapefile layers, all in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326): National_Boundary with two features, Pakistan and IIOJK, so the outline can be drawn with or without the disputed territory; Provincial_Boundary with eight features (Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, Gilgit Baltistan, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, the Federal Capital Territory and IIOJK) with areas in square kilometres in geographic, UTM 41N and UTM 43N terms; District_Boundary with 161 districts; and Tehsil_Boundary with 554 tehsils.

The IIOJK polygon and the national and provincial outlines that include it were digitised by Muhammad Taimoor Ashfaq against the Survey of Pakistan political map and merged with district and tehsil lines derived from the OCHA Pakistan and Population Census Organisation boundary data. Each layer carries the same metadata in ArcGIS (.shp.xml) and QGIS (.qmd) form, so the source, creator and licence travel with the file.
requirements: Any GIS that reads shapefiles: QGIS, ArcGIS Pro, ArcMap, GeoPandas, R sf
Reproject to UTM 42N (EPSG:32642) or a national equal-area projection before measuring areas; the stored areas were computed in UTM 41N and 43N
Districts reflect the 2017 census-era boundaries; districts created since then (for example in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan) are not split out
Cite as: Muhammad Taimoor Ashfaq (2021), Pakistan administrative boundaries including IIOJK, Arid Society of GIS, with the OCHA/PCO base acknowledged

name: Galiyat boundary, Galiyat Development Authority jurisdiction
description: The Galiyat Development Authority's area of responsibility in Abbottabad district, from Murree Road through Ayubia, Nathia Gali and Thandiani, as one clean polygon. Shapefile in WGS 84 with metadata.
about: The Galiyat is the hill-station belt of Abbottabad district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Ayubia, Nathia Gali, Dunga Gali, Khaira Gali, Changla Gali, Bara Gali and Thandiani, on the ridge that runs north from Murree. Since 1996 it has been administered for planning, tourism, building control and services by the Galiyat Development Authority (GDA), a provincial body whose jurisdiction is a planning boundary rather than a tehsil or union council. Because it is not a census or revenue unit, it does not appear in the national administrative datasets, and anyone studying tourism, forest change, landslides or construction in the Galiyat has had to redraw it.

This file is that boundary as a single polygon of about 636 square kilometres with a perimeter of about 221 kilometres, in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326). The attribute table holds the name, authority, province, district, area, perimeter, source, creator and year, replacing the empty 27-field land use template the original digitising carried.

The boundary was digitised in May 2025 during the Galiyat land use survey against the GDA's notified limits and high-resolution imagery, and was cleaned, documented and published by Muhammad Taimoor Ashfaq for the Arid Society of GIS. Metadata travels with the file in ArcGIS (.shp.xml) and QGIS (.qmd) form.
requirements: Any GIS that reads shapefiles: QGIS, ArcGIS Pro, ArcMap, GeoPandas, R sf
Use with the Pakistan administrative boundaries dataset above for tehsil and district context; the Galiyat crosses tehsil lines
Areas were computed on the WGS 84 sphere; reproject to UTM 43N (EPSG:32643) for engineering-grade measurements
This is the GDA jurisdiction, not the Ayubia National Park or the Galiyat forest division; those have their own, smaller boundaries
Cite as: Muhammad Taimoor Ashfaq (2025), Galiyat boundary, Galiyat Development Authority jurisdiction, Arid Society of GIS

name: SRTM 30 m DEM, Pakistan mosaic
description: Void-filled SRTM 1 arc-second tiles mosaicked for the whole country, GeoTIFF, WGS84.

name: ESA WorldCover 10 m land cover, Pakistan
description: 2021 global land cover at 10 m clipped to Pakistan, with class legend and QGIS style file.

name: CHIRPS monthly rainfall, Pakistan, 1981 to 2025
description: Monthly precipitation rasters clipped to Pakistan, plus a district-level summary table.

name: OpenStreetMap roads and places, Pakistan
description: Roads, railways, waterways and populated places extracted from the Geofabrik Pakistan extract, GeoPackage.

name: WorldPop population 100 m, Pakistan 2020
description: Constrained population count raster, with district aggregates and 2023 census totals for comparison.

name: Society map layout template
description: QGIS print layout with the institute logo, north arrow, scale bar, legend and metadata block, A4 and A3.

name: Final year project report template
description: Word and LaTeX templates following the institute's formatting rules, with a sample chapter structure.

name: InVEST Workbench
description: Stanford's free ecosystem-services modelling suite: carbon storage, sediment and nutrient retention, water yield, habitat quality, pollination and coastal vulnerability, run from one desktop app on your own rasters and shapefiles.
about: InVEST (Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs) is a family of spatial models from Stanford's Natural Capital Project that put numbers and maps on what landscapes do for people.
Models include carbon storage, sediment delivery, nutrient runoff, water yield, habitat quality, pollination, coastal vulnerability, urban cooling and urban flood risk.
Inputs are ordinary GIS data (a land-use raster, a DEM, a watershed boundary, a lookup table); outputs are rasters and tables you open in QGIS or ArcGIS.
The Workbench wraps every model in one app: pick a model, fill a form that validates inputs before the run, watch the log, open the results.
Every run is reproducible from Python through the natcap.invest package, which is how most published studies script scenario comparisons.

Quickest route to a final year project with a policy angle: a Sentinel-2 or Landsat land-cover change map feeds straight into Carbon, Sediment Delivery Ratio or Habitat Quality. Projects on Margalla Hills, the Potohar plateau, the Sindh mangroves and the Indus delta have used it.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, or macOS 11 or later; no Linux build, use the Python package there
8 GB RAM; large DEMs and the sediment model benefit from 16 GB
About 1 GB of disk space for the install, plus 400 MB if you add the sample data
Inputs in a projected coordinate system with metres as the unit; geographic WGS 84 rasters must be reprojected first
Model-specific tables (biophysical lookup tables, species sensitivity tables) prepared as CSV; the sample data shows the exact columns

figures.caption: InVEST Workbench main screen: the model list on the left, recent runs on the right. Screenshot from the InVEST User Guide (Natural Capital Project).
